title: Melody | Slow paced, zen based, ASMR, zero gravity/zero friction, physics/puzzle game.
author: Camenwolf
selftext:
This is a game idea I've had for literally 30 years.  I built a prototype of it in Unity around 2016 or so.  I got it into a demo-able state and it was fun, but tapered off of it because so... much... WORK.   Agentic coding tools have finally allowed me to realize the vision.  It's a physics/puzzle based game that uses primitive shapes, so it's not going to blow your hair back with mind numbing graphics or anything.  It's a simple gameplay loop, but (I feel) a very difficult game to master.  In a way I'm almost glad I never finished it back then, because I honestly think this was meant to be a browser based game.  Also back then I would not have released the editor because I was building for platforms on which they have have been problematic.

The premise that I was going for was an ASMR, zen based game that rewards you for remaining calm and centered as you play and absolutely punishes you if you lose your temper or your patience.

* A level editor to design and publish your own levels for others to play
* A five star rating system to rate community levels and official levels
* Tracked playlist progress so you don't lose credit for the levels you've completed between sessions.
* Custom playlists to build your own playlists of your favorite community and official levels.
* Personal records for best times
* A leaderboard for community best times and leaderboard placement
* Custom Rulesets - Rulesets are collections of properties that dictate how the game plays.  Properties dictate almost everything from friction, air resistance, ball size, restitution of surfaces, mass, acceleration, on and on.  You can use custom properties in the editor to create a game that plays nothing like the original Melody.  But if you use a standard ruleset, then other players will know "Okay, this is a custom level but it plays similarly to the official levels.  It's not going to be doing crazy s\*\*\*!" 

I built it almost entirely in Codex using the high reasoning 5.x model (the model changed a couple of times during development).  The game and editor are built in Phaser 3.90.0.  The website is a single page vanilla javascript application, although I wish I had built it in react.  To convert it now will take a monumental effort, although I'm still considering it.

I'm calling it "Early Access" because I don't know if later I would want to want to put ads on the site or something later if it were to become popular for some weird reason.  I do have a place where people can tip with Kofi.  I hope that doesn't make it some sort of "commercial" product or whatever.  I can promise you that not a single person has... nor likely will, but I put it out there anyway, so if that's breaking the rules, let me know.

The main thing, PLEASE tell me if it's any fun?  I know many people will not enjoy it based solely on the kind of game it is.  It is slow... very slow, methodical, requires patience and calm.  But if you are the type of person who likes puzzle games, billiards, or like slow paced ASMR type games, please give it a try and tell me if you think it is any good or what you think I can improve.

Also, if someone wanted try the editor and build a level, I'd love to hear your opinion of the editor.  It's the exact same editor I used to build all of the official levels, and I'll bet a million dollars that many people could use my editor and build levels 10X better than what I've made.

If you've read this far THANK YOU!  You are freaking AWESOME!!!  PLEASE play it one time.
